tagline: The quietest of the inhabited Princes' Islands — rugged, unhurried, with pine forests reaching the sea and an authentic village life that Büyükada no longer has.

items.name: İskele Kafesi
items.description: The simple café right at the ferry landing. Order çay, watch the boat leave, and feel the island pace immediately take hold.

items.name: Çarşı Çay Bahçeleri
items.description: Small tea gardens in the village centre near the church. Very local, very quiet. This is what Büyükada used to feel like.

items.name: Kalpazankaya Restaurant
items.description: A legendary fish restaurant on the rocks at the water's edge — one of the most special dining spots in the entire Istanbul area. Tables literally hang over the sea.
items.tip: Book ahead even on weekdays. Walk or take a water taxi from the ferry landing — it's not accessible by land vehicle.

items.name: Ada Lokantalari
items.description: Simple, honest meyhane and lokanta restaurants in the village serving fish mezes and grilled seafood. Very local crowd.

items.name: Hristos Tepesi (Christ Hill) Walk
items.description: A scenic walk through pine forest to the hilltop chapel with views across all the Princes' Islands and the Istanbul skyline.
items.tip: The walk up takes about 40 minutes. Bring water — there's nothing on the way up.

items.name: Sait Faik Müzesi
items.description: The home-museum of Sait Faik Abasıyanık, one of Turkey's greatest short story writers, who lived here. Small, intimate, and very moving.

items.name: Island Perimeter Walk
items.description: Unlike Büyükada, Burgazada is small enough to walk around entirely on foot in 2-3 hours. Pine forests, rocky coves, and almost no other tourists.

tips: Ferry from Kabataş or Bostancı — Burgazada is the second stop after Kınalıada. Total journey about 60-75 minutes.
Far fewer visitors than Büyükada — weekends are busy but never overwhelming. Weekdays are practically deserted.
There are no cars and no bicycles for rent. You walk everywhere. Bring comfortable shoes.
The island has one small market and a few restaurants. Don't rely on ATMs — bring enough cash.
